saints.name: St. Lawrence
saints.title: Deacon and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A deacon of Rome who, ordered to hand over the Church’s treasures, gathered the poor and said, “These are the treasures of the Church”…
biography: Born about 225 at Huesca in Roman Spain, Lawrence met there, by tradition, the future Pope Sixtus II and followed him to Rome, where he was made archdeacon, the first of the city's seven deacons, charged with the Church's treasury and the care of the poor.

When Sixtus was seized and beheaded on 6 August 258 in Valerian's persecution, the prefect of Rome demanded the Church's wealth. Lawrence asked three days, spent them distributing everything to the needy, then presented the poor, the crippled, and the blind, declaring these the treasures of the Church.

Ancient tradition, sung by the poet Prudentius, holds that he was roasted alive on a gridiron and in his agony cheerfully bade his executioners turn him over, for one side was done. He died on 10 August 258 and was buried on the Via Tiburtina, where Constantine built a basilica in his honour.

His name stands in the Roman Canon of the Mass, and he is among the most honoured martyrs of Rome. He is patron of deacons, whose ministry he bore; of cooks, because of the gridiron's fire; and of the poor, whom he named the Church's true riches.
saints.knownFor: “The treasures of the Church are the poor”; martyrdom on the gridiron.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 10 August
